newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk nickel union says it adopts strike plan.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk nickel union says it adopts strike plan.

text.p: Workers at the flagship plant of Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group have adopted a proposal to strike over wage arrears, Boris Degtyaryov, deputy head of the plant's United Trade Union committee said on Monday.

"It (the committee) has adopted its legimitate right to hold a strike," he told Reuters from the Arctic town of Norilsk where the plant is situated. "The company management has 10 days in which to resolve the situation."

Degtyaryov said the union committee took the decision to adopt the strike plan at a meeting on March 1. He said that phone lines connecting the remote town with Moscow were down on Saturday and Sunday.

He said a 17-member committee has been set up to coordinate strike action if it were to go ahead. The exact timing of any action and the number of workers involved would be decided by the coordinating committee.
But Degtyaryov said a strike would involve a minimum of 50,000 workers involved in metals production at the plant, up to the plant's entire workforce of 120,000.
He also said that the committee would do everything in its power to continue with "conciliatory procedures" to resolve the disagreement before a strike is called.
"A perfect outcome would be that if all our (the union's) legitimate demands were met, there would be no strike," he said.
Workers are demanding that salary and holiday arrears of around 900 billion roubles be paid. The Norilsk group also owes about 1.2 trillion roubles to various budgets.
Workers are also demanding wages be increased by what a RAO Norilsky Nickel spokesman said earlier would cost the company 70 billion roubles a month.

RAO Norilsky Nickel is a major supplier of nickel, cobalt and platinum group metals to world markets. Last year the main metals plant produced 100,000 tonnes of nickel from the group's total nickel output of 177,185 tonnes.
